Building on arbitrary-mask conditioning in diffusion models, we jointly train a differentiable Top-K selector with the generator so that anchor choices minimize denoising NLL and temporal drift, supervised by large-scale highlight/summarization signals and optionally guided by language to align anchors with a user-described storyline. The selector borrows joint, non-redundant coverage objectives from frame-selection methods and adapts the conditioning schedule online via uncertainty, interleaving anchor-conditioned and free denoising steps. This event-anchored scheduling improves coherence and compute-efficiency over heuristic or uniform conditioning baselines on long-duration datasets.

result.text: Recent work shows jailbreaks that bypass safety can also degrade model capabilities, but defenses rarely monitor this shift. We propose Sentinel Probes: interleaving lightweight, content-agnostic micro-probes (e.g., quick reasoning, calibration, and consistency checks) during a conversation to estimate real-time capability drift and trigger recovery (state reset, safety re-grounding, or conditional routing) when a jailbreak-induced mode shift is detected. We evaluate across standardized jailbreak suites and forbidden-information metrics, extend to agentic and code-completion settings with context-specific probes, and quantify both detection AUC and retained helpfulness on capability testbeds. This turns capability degradation from a hidden side-effect into a detectable signal for robust, low-latency jailbreak mitigation.

result.text: We propose delay-robust adversarial SSP, addressing stochastic shortest path learning with unknown transitions, adversarially chosen per-episode costs, and arbitrary, obliviously chosen delays in revealing trajectory and cost feedback. The algorithm maintains optimism-based confidence sets for transitions as in state-of-the-art SSP learners but updates them through a delayed credit-queue that logs episode models and attributes late-arriving feedback to the correct past planning states; it augments planning with delay-aware step-size schedules and optional skipping of extremely delayed feedback to keep variance controlled. We conjecture high-probability regret O~(sqrt(S^2 A D T* (K + D_tot))) under full-information delays and O~((S^3 A^2 D T*)^{1/3} (K + D_tot)^{2/3}) in the bandit-adversarial case, with horizon-free variants replacing T* by B* via skewed empirical models, and refined bounds when selectively skipping highly delayed episodes. Technically this blends optimistic SSP estimation with occupancy-measure style delayed aggregation and bandit delay adaptivity, yielding the first instance-dependent guarantees for SSP under adversarial costs and unbounded delays.

result.text: The paper addresses why Graph Neural Networks struggle to propagate and preserve useful information across graphs—manifesting as over-smoothing (node features becoming indistinguishable) and over-squashing (long-range signals being compressed and lost). Its key insight is that both pathologies are governed by local graph geometry expressed via Ollivier-Ricci curvature: positive curvature regions promote feature mixing and thus over-smoothing, while negative curvature regions concentrate and distort flows, causing over-squashing. Building on this, the authors derive theoretical links between curvature and message-passing dynamics and introduce Batch Ollivier-Ricci Flow, a curvature-aware graph rewiring algorithm that iteratively adjusts edges to normalize local curvature and thereby mitigate both over-smoothing and over-squashing simultaneously.

result.text: The paper tackles the challenge of sample-efficiently training reinforcement learning agents to generalize across varying problem instances (contexts) within a domain. The key insight is that state-value estimates during training contain useful signals for automatically selecting which contexts to train on next, enabling an adaptive curriculum that starts with easier or more informative contexts and progressively focuses on harder ones. The proposed method, Self-Paced Context Evaluation (SPaCE), implements an online, low-overhead curriculum generator that uses value-function information from any value-based RL agent to score and prioritize contexts for training, and it can be applied modularly on top of existing agents. result.text: The paper tackles the challenge of running large pretrained LLMs on resource-constrained devices by eliminating expensive dense multiplications while preserving accuracy without full retraining. The key insight is that weight matrices can be post-training reparameterized into binary matrices with group-wise scaling so multiplications become hardware-friendly shifts and adds, and that jointly minimizing errors in both weights and output activations plus allocating bits per layer according to sensitivity can recover accuracy. The method quantizes each weight into binary components plus group scalings, re-expresses matrix multiplies as shifts between activations and scalars plus add operations guided by the binary masks, and optimizes a multi-objective loss to reduce reparameterization-induced errors while automatically assigning bit-widths across layers. result.text: The paper addresses the problem of learning classifiers that remain fair when the test distribution differs from the training distribution via covariate shift (inputs change but labels given inputs remain governed by the same conditional distribution), a setting where conventional fairness methods that assume iid data can fail. The key insight is to cast fairness under covariate shift as a robust optimization problem: enforce fairness on the (unlabeled) target distribution while controlling worst-case test performance by constraining candidate predictors to match certain statistical properties of the source data and respecting the invariant conditional label law. result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of injecting structured knowledge from knowledge graphs into pre-trained language models without incurring the heavy retrieval and encoding costs that hinder real-world deployment, especially for high-speed inference. Its key insight is to focus injection on knowledge-aware long-tail entities and to decompose knowledge incorporation across pre-training, fine-tuning, and inference by replacing long-tail entity embeddings with lightweight "pseudo token representations" derived from relevant relation triples and enforcing understanding via a relational knowledge decoding objective. Its key insight is to relax full factorial independence to pairwise factorized support: instead of forcing independent distributions, enforce that each factor’s support combines in a Cartesian-product-like way by minimizing a Hausdorff distance between the joint support and a factorized-support approximation. result.text: The paper addresses open-vocabulary video instance segmentation (OpenVIS), i.e., detecting, segmenting, and tracking instances of arbitrary categories in video without being limited to training-time classes. result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of training deep spiking neural networks (SNNs) efficiently and online: current high-performance methods like backpropagation through time (BPTT) with surrogate gradients demand large time-dependent memory, lack biological plausibility, and conflict with on-chip online learning, while spike-representation approaches either are not online or require many time steps. The key insight is that BPTT can be reformulated into a forward-in-time algorithm that tracks presynaptic activity and uses instantaneous losses to compute updates that both (a) require only constant memory independent of the number of time steps and (b) yield descent directions theoretically comparable to those from spike-representation gradients under feedforward and recurrent conditions. The method, called online training through time (OTTT), derives online gradient estimates from BPTT by maintaining local presynaptic traces and composing updates into a three-factor Hebbian-like rule, enabling efficient GPU training and biologically/plausibly implementable on-chip learning; empirically OTTT achieves strong performance on CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet and CIFAR10-DVS with few time steps.

args.text: We propose a Fractional Fourier Neural Operator (FrFNO) that replaces the fixed Fourier projection in FNO with a learned mixture of fractional orders, yielding non-stationary, chirped basis functions that better capture advection- and dispersion-dominated PDE dynamics. Concretely, each operator layer computes K fractional-domain projections with per-mode, input-conditioned order parameters and low-rank spectral weights, realized efficiently via chirp–FFT–chirp factorizations and fused matmul-style kernels, before mapping back to physical space. To preserve local sharp structures, we couple these global FrFT integral layers with localized differential/integral operator blocks in a hybrid, resolution-agnostic architecture. We hypothesize substantial error reductions on turbulent Navier–Stokes, shallow-water, and wave equations over FNO baselines with modest overhead amortized by FFT-based FRFT implementations.

EdgeDecentGS: a fully decentralized, fault-tolerant training framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting on heterogeneous, intermittently connected devices. It adopts DOGS-style spatial decomposition but replaces the master-driven ADMM with boundary-only consensus performed via scheduled one-peer exponential graphs and Moshpit-style averaging, enabling near-exact model alignment without a reliable high-speed fabric. Communication is further reduced by Grendel’s sparsity—nodes gossip only Gaussians whose screen-space footprints intersect neighbors’ pixel shards—and by LEAD-style compressed exchanges with error-corrected tracking, stabilizing optimization under heavy quantization. This yields city-scale 3DGS that scales beyond single clusters, preserving quality while improving wall-clock convergence under churn and load imbalance.

result.text: We propose Conformally-Weighted Self-Consistency (CWSC), a black-box uncertainty method that turns LLM agreement patterns into prediction sets or risk thresholds with PAC-style guarantees under distribution shift. We train this module by distilling refusal behavior from a safety-aligned text model onto the vision path using curated safe-instruction data and benign counterparts, augmented with hard negatives from typographic-image prompts and encoder-targeted adversarial images, with a contrastive loss that collapses harmful cues across modalities while preserving task semantics. At inference, we (i) project visual features through the learned safety nullspace and (ii) gate generation with a calibrated safety score, regularized by OCR cycle-consistency so image-rendered text yields the same safety decision as its transcription. The framework predicts breakpoints in the scaling curve as bisection bandwidth, batch size, or sequence length vary, and prescribes adaptive controllers that adjust routing and granularity online to stay on the bandwidth- and compute-optimal frontier. result.text: The paper addresses the threat of clean-label data poisoning—stealthy modifications to a small fraction of training data that cause a trained neural network to adopt attacker-chosen behaviors—by replacing prior hand-crafted heuristics with an optimization-driven approach. The key insight is to frame poison crafting as a bilevel optimization problem where the inner loop trains the victim model on poisoned data and the outer loop optimizes the poison examples to induce a desired misclassification, enabling principled, targeted attacks that transfer across models and settings. The authors introduce MetaPoison, a first-order approximate solver that efficiently backpropagates through (or approximates) the training procedure to update poison pixels, and demonstrate its effectiveness and robustness across fine-tuning and end-to-end training, achieving high attack success rates with only ~1% poisoned data, flexible target-label manipulation, and real-world efficacy against services like Google Cloud AutoML Vision.

result.text: We propose DEON-Adaptive Trust-Projected PPO, which safely reuses off-policy data by combining exact per-state trust-region projections for Gaussian policies with a clipping range that adapts to measured off-policyness. Concretely, we insert differentiable projection layers that enforce a per-state KL trust region during forward passes and modulate the surrogate’s clipping bounds as a monotone function of an off-policy metric (e.g., DEON), tightening when data are far from on-policy and relaxing when they are close. The step size and importance weighting are calibrated using generalized off-policy policy improvement bounds, yielding updates whose distances and guarantees mirror PPO’s while expanding the effective data reuse regime. We hypothesize this improves sample efficiency and stability over PPO, Off-Policy PPO, G-PPO-SR, and sigmoid-surrogate variants across continuous-control benchmarks.

result.text: The paper tackles the instability and reliance on manual design in role-based multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), where existing methods either assume predefined role structures or require expert tuning to decompose complex tasks. Its key insight is to cast role discovery as a hierarchical action-space clustering problem grounded in Structural Information principles, enabling automatic, principled extraction of stable and informative roles via an optimal encoding tree. The proposed SIRD method comprises structuralization, sparsification, and optimization modules that build and prune an encoding tree to produce abstract roles, and it is integrated into a general SR-MARL framework that can work with various value-function factorization algorithms. Empirical results on StarCraft II micromanagement show that SR-MARL yields modest to substantial gains in average win rate and markedly reduces variance across easy, hard, and super-hard scenarios compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

result.text: The paper addresses Generalized Category Discovery (GCD), where a dataset has both labeled and unlabeled images and the goal is to cluster the unlabeled images into both known and novel classes consistent with the taxonomy implied by the labeled set. The key insight is that existing benchmarks often admit a single natural partition, so models can succeed by unsupervised grouping rather than by extrapolating the labeled taxonomy; to reveal this, the authors introduce Clevr-4, a synthetic dataset with four equally valid mutually orthogonal partitions (shape, texture, color, count) that forces methods to follow the labeled taxonomy. They show strong unsupervised methods fail on Clevr-4 and identify weaknesses in prior GCD algorithms, then propose μGCD, a simple mean-teacher–based method that leverages consistency regularization from representation learning to align unlabeled clustering with the labeled taxonomy; μGCD substantially outperforms baselines on Clevr-4 and achieves state-of-the-art results on the real-data Semantic Shift Benchmark.

result.text: The paper addresses the mismatch between rigid group-equivariant convolutional networks and real data that often exhibits only partial or layer-varying symmetries, which can hurt performance when full equivariance is imposed. Its key insight is that equivariance need not be binary—networks can and should learn the degree of equivariance per layer and per transformation range (including subsets of continuous groups) to better match the statistics of the data. To realize this, the authors introduce Partial G-CNNs that parameterize and learn layer-wise partial and full equivariance to discrete and continuous groups (and combinations) as part of training, thereby interpolating between standard CNNs and fully equivariant G-CNNs. Empirically, Partial G-CNNs retain full equivariance when beneficial (e.g., rotated MNIST) but relax it when harmful (e.g., distinguishing 6 vs 9 or on natural images), matching or exceeding G-CNN performance.

result.text: VectorGlyph Diffusion bridges the gap between diffusion-based text rendering and true typography by inserting a differentiable vector-font head into the denoising loop. The model predicts per-glyph vector outlines (e.g., Bezier/SDF parameters), kerning, and homography-aware placement that are rasterized by a differentiable renderer and fused into cross-attention; training uses a hybrid loss combining denoising, OCR/text-perceptual alignment, and outline-level Chamfer/IoU to ensure stroke fidelity for small text and low-resource scripts. At inference, we alternate denoising with a lightweight optimizer over outlines and placements to enforce exact legibility, perspective consistency, and occlusion handling, yielding plug-and-play editing and robust in-the-wild text insertion. This unifies and extends prior glyph/position conditioning and stroke-aware objectives while providing an explicit, editable vector representation that remains crisp under scaling and compression.

args.text: We propose a montage-equivariant continuous EEG encoder that models the scalp as a spherical neural field with group-equivariant attention over geodesic distances, enabling a single model to handle arbitrary electrode layouts and unseen montages while extending unified-topology pretraining. A dual-path design fuses time-domain features with a covariance-based SPD manifold stream equipped with manifold-aware attention to improve robustness to nonstationarity and yield more stable, interpretable representations. We pretrain with mixed self-supervised objectives—masked channel/time modeling plus contrastive subgraph/augmentation across random electrode subsets and sessions—to learn montage-invariant yet instance-adaptive relational structure. Fine-tuned for seizure detection/localization and emotion recognition, this approach is expected to improve cross-dataset transfer and rare-class performance over discrete-topology GNN SSL baselines.

result.text: The paper addresses the lack of rigorous, general approximation-error guarantees for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and operator-learning architectures (e.g., DeepONets, FNOs) when used to approximate solutions and solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs). Its key insight is that existing approximation results for standard neural networks can be systematically lifted to more complex, PDE-oriented architectures and to physics-informed formulations, yielding provable error bounds that hold for broad classes of PDEs and operators and that can avoid the curse of dimensionality in relevant settings. Methodologically, the authors develop a unifying framework that composes known neural network approximation theorems with stability and regularity estimates for PDE solution maps, producing explicit bounds for PINNs, physics-informed DeepONets and FNOs, and for the first time deriving rigorous approximation-error guarantees for physics-informed operator learning, with concrete application to nonlinear parabolic problems.

args.text: We propose Hierarchical Tree-aware Preference Optimization (HTPO) for tool-augmented LLMs: instead of pairwise stepwise preferences, we learn from entire sampled action trees with structured, multiway, token-aware supervision. Concretely, we use a single Tree-Planner pass to sample diverse complete plans, induce local n-way rankings among sibling branches at each decision node using task success, latency, and tool-cost metrics, and train with node-local PRO while applying TDPO-style forward-KL token-level regularization on the action prefixes; the DPO trade-off β is dynamically calibrated per batch from ranking margins and entropy. An active selection loop prioritizes uncertain/high-entropy decision nodes for additional execution and labeling, improving label efficiency. HTPO should yield more reliable tool-usage policies with better generalization to unseen APIs and lower token/tool costs than iterative loop training that ignores multi-branch structure.

args.text: We propose LAMP: a layout-to-action multimodal program inducer that, given a UI/web screenshot and a natural-language instruction, jointly predicts HTML/CSS code and an executable interaction program whose actions (e.g., click, type, scroll) are grounded to the predicted DOM via selectors, enabling end-to-end automation and accessibility. LAMP builds on screenshot-to-HTML pretraining and instruction-tuned web-to-code for faithful code synthesis, augments with an instruction-aware visual querying module and a focus-conditioned pathway to localize task-relevant regions, and trains with render-and-compare consistency plus script-execution feedback. Structurally, it first predicts a coarse region-level layout skeleton before completing HTML-like DSL code, then compiles action primitives against the induced DOM. We hypothesize this yields stronger generalization and robustness on multi-step UI tasks than vision-only or code-only baselines.

result.text: The paper addresses building general-purpose agents that can solve a wide variety of tasks by overcoming limited task-specific policies and heterogeneous state/action spaces. The key insight is to reframe sequential decision-making as text-conditioned video generation: given a language-encoded goal, a planner generates future frames that depict a visual plan, and control actions are then extracted from those synthesized videos, enabling combinatorial generalization to novel goals and unified representation across different environments. Methodologically, the authors train a policy-as-video model that conditions video prediction on pretrained language embeddings and large internet video data, uses the generated frames as a medium for cross-task and cross-robot transfer, and decodes control commands from the predicted visual trajectories to execute manipulation tasks on real robots.

args.text: On-Policy Conformal Autofocusing couples a proposal policy (generative optimizer) with an oracle and enforces deployment-calibrated uncertainty under the optimizer’s evolving query distribution. We estimate density ratios between the current query distribution and the offline training set to reweight oracle updates and impose importance-weighted conformal calibration constraints so the oracle outputs intervals that remain valid on-policy. The proposal policy is initialized from offline trajectories and then fine-tuned in an RL framing of sequential design to maximize predicted performance minus a penalty for interval width, yielding a performatively stable operating point. result.text: The paper addresses the problem of "over-squashing" in graph neural networks, where information from distant nodes gets compressed and distorted during message passing, limiting GNN performance on tasks needing long-range interactions; this is commonly attributed to graph bottlenecks but lacked a precise formulation. args.text: We propose a Relightable Large Reconstruction Model (R-LRM) that maps a single in-the-wild image to a disentangled, relightable asset: geometry (SDF/mesh), spatially-varying BRDF, and an HDR environment map. Concretely, starting from a BirdSet-pretrained classifier, we freeze its classifier head and adapt the encoder plus the frontend on unlabeled target audio by (i) an audio-MAE loss on high-ratio masked patches and (ii) enforcing agreement between encoder predictions across augmentations and pseudo-tokens from a frozen acoustic tokenizer; every few epochs we refresh the tokenizer by distilling discrete labels from the adapted encoder on high-confidence segments (BEATs-style), all without source data. This hybrid SSL-plus-token framework should outperform entropy/pseudo-label SFDA baselines under real bioacoustic shifts while preserving high-level semantics via token supervision and handling channel shift via the learnable frontend. We will evaluate on BirdSet covariate-shift splits and include HEAR-style embedding transfer tests to assess whether the adapted representations generalize beyond species identification.

We propose a mechanism-based predictor for Broken Neural Scaling Law breakpoints: breaks occur when training crosses optimizer and architecture regime boundaries, specifically when the step-size–to–curvature ratio and effective SGD noise exceed Edge-of-Stability/unstable-convergence thresholds, or when MoE granularity/routing reallocations shift the compute–error tradeoff. Leveraging analyses of EOS dynamics and high-dimensional SGD, and MoE granularity scaling, we specify a multi-axis piecewise power law whose break locations are explicit functions of η·λ_max, batch-size/data-reuse noise scale, and expert granularity/load variance; this yields conditions for when compute-optimal policies switch from “add steps” to “add parameters/experts.” We outline experiments that jointly track sharpness, noise scale, and routing imbalance across scales to fit these breakpoint predictors and validate their extrapolations, enabling proactive curricula (step size, batch, and granularity schedules) that avoid suboptimal pre-break regimes.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of scaling dataset distillation—specifically trajectory-matching-based methods (MTT)—to large-scale datasets like ImageNet-1K, where prior approaches fail due to excessive memory use and poor convergence with many classes. The key insight is that the unrolled gradient used by MTT can be computed exactly with constant memory complexity, enabling a ~6x reduction in memory footprint, and that class-rich datasets benefit from a novel soft label assignment to improve convergence. Methodologically, the authors derive a constant-memory procedure to compute the unrolled SGD gradient, integrate a soft-label scheme for per-class synthetic images, and apply this at scale to distill ImageNet-1K up to 50 images per class on a single GPU. The resulting algorithm achieves new state-of-the-art distilled-data performance on ImageNet-1K—using only 4.2% of the original data with a 5.9% accuracy gap to full-data training and an 18.2% absolute gain over prior SOTA.

result.text: The paper addresses open-vocabulary video instance segmentation (OpenVIS), i.e., detecting, segmenting, and tracking instances of arbitrary categories in video without being limited to training-time classes. Its key insight is that strong open-vocabulary capabilities can be achieved by combining class-agnostic, recall-focused mask proposals with instance-centric open-vocabulary token encoders and a tracking formulation that predicts future instance tokens rather than relying on closed-set identity labels. result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of learning policies for multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) that must adapt to changing, potentially continuous preference vectors without training and storing separate policies for every preference. The key insight is to train a single universal network conditioned on preference vectors that can represent the Pareto front across the entire preference space, using preferences to directly guide parameter updates and a parallelized data-collection scheme to boost sample efficiency. The method, called Preference-Driven MORL (PD-MORL), conditions a single policy network on preference inputs, updates network parameters with preference-weighted objectives, and employs a novel parallelization strategy to improve learning efficiency in continuous control tasks. Empirically, PD-MORL yields substantially larger hypervolume (up to 25% improvement) while using an order of magnitude fewer trainable parameters than prior approaches.

The paper tackles the challenge of long-horizon decision-making from pixels, where current agents struggle to decompose tasks into subgoals and plan across thousands of steps without manually specified goal spaces. Its key insight is that planning can be done effectively and interpretable if a learned latent world model provides a compact space in which a high-level policy selects latent goals and a low-level policy executes them, with the model able to decode latent goals back into images for visualization. The method, called Director, trains a world model from pixels, uses model-based planning in latent space for the high-level controller to maximize task and exploration rewards, and concurrently trains a goal-conditioned low-level policy to reach latent goals; this hierarchical setup enables efficient exploration and long-horizon control. Empirically, Director outperforms prior exploration methods on sparse-reward 3D maze and robot navigation tasks without privileged state, and generalizes across visual control domains, Atari, and DMLab.

result.text: The paper compares two approaches for learning from human preferences—reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) which learns an explicit reward model then optimizes a policy, and direct preference optimization (DPO) which directly fits a policy to pairwise preferences—focusing on log-linear policies and linear rewards. The key insight is that under this parametric setting one can derive statistical minimax bounds and convergence rates that reveal distinct behaviors: both methods admit exponentially fast convergence under exact or approximate optimization, but DPO can avoid a constant asymptotic error when the true reward is misspecified by appropriately tuning the regularization temperature, whereas RLHF suffers a persistent model-misspecification gap. A lightweight selector learns to pick a complementary subset of frames under differentiable compute constraints (top-k/knapsack) given a target FLOP/latency budget and a task token, supervised jointly by downstream task losses and large-scale implicit highlight signals. args.text: We propose a tri-modal, weakly supervised AMT framework that learns from unaligned symbolic scores and large-scale captioned music audio by jointly optimizing (1) a NoteEM-style score–audio aligner, (2) an MT3-style sequence-to-sequence transcriber, and (3) an audio–text consistency head. Concretely, we initialize the audio encoder with MERT and impose CLAP-based alignment between predicted captions and audio, while using DISCO-10M’s captions to constrain pseudo-label filtering; training couples soft score–audio alignments with transcription losses and an embedding-agreement loss across augmentations (pitch shift/time-stretch). To stabilize learning, we enforce monotonicity and locality with dynamic-programming alignment constraints inspired by lyric–melody alignment, and use agreement across the three heads to select high-confidence pseudo-labels. Beyond improved low-resource instrument AMT, the model enables instruction-conditioned selective transcription (e.g., “only guitar”) by gating the transcriber with the caption head at inference.

Phase-Gated Dual-Channel Attention: each head computes two parallel score matrices—content-only and position-only with separate projections as in TUPE—and mixes them with a learned gate that is regularized to increase semantic weight as sample complexity or layer depth grows, guided online by a decomposition of hidden states into positional vectors. For inference far beyond the training window, the positional branch uses ALiBi or FFT-exact relative positional bias to remain stable, while the semantic branch prunes diagonals to save compute without hurting expressivity. A training-free variant estimates the gate from the ratio of positional-vector energy to content energy and swaps in extrapolated/replaced positional vectors when needed. This unifies theoretical phase-transition insights with practical long-context extensions to yield interpretable, length-robust attention.

result.text: The paper investigates the privacy risk that Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems pose by showing that instruction-tuned LMs can be coerced via prompt injection to verbatim-leak documents stored in their retrieval datastores. The key insight is that modern instruction-following LMs often fail to robustly condition on external context and instead heed adversarial prompts, so attackers can exploit position and instruction-following biases to induce the model to regurgitate retrieved passages. The authors demonstrate this empirically across many popular LMs (e.g., Llama2, Mistral, Vicuna, Qwen, Platypus2) and production GPT-based custom models, quantify how RAG setup and model scale affect extractability, and show that simple mitigation—eliminating position bias in retrieval conditioning—substantially reduces leakage. They further present practical attacks that recover large fractions of text from real datastores (e.g., 41% of a 77k-word book) with few queries and recommend architectural changes to reduce the vulnerability.

result.text: The paper tackles the challenge of low-bit quantization for large language models, where rare but large-magnitude "outlier" activations—especially extreme "massive" outliers—cause severe accuracy degradation. result.text: The paper tackles the problem of inefficient and brittle scaling studies caused by common use of cosine learning-rate schedules, which tie a model’s training dynamics to a fixed duration and force many costly, bespoke runs to explore different compute budgets. result.text: The paper tackles improving cut selection in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) solvers, noting that effective heuristics must decide which cuts to prefer, how many to select, and in what order to apply them. The key insight is that cut selection is naturally a hierarchical sequential decision problem—choice of count and an ordered subset both matter for solver performance—so learning both levels jointly will outperform methods that treat only preferences or counts independently. They propose HEM, a two-level hierarchical sequence model trained with reinforcement learning: a high-level controller predicts the number of cuts to pick, and a low-level sequence-to-sequence policy selects an ordered subset of that size from candidate cuts. Empirical results on synthetic and large-scale real-world MILPs (including MIPLIB 2017) show HEM improves solver efficiency and generalizes to substantially larger instances than seen during training.

args.text: I propose Hessian-guided probabilistic bitplane PV-Tuning for 1–2-bit LLMs: represent each vector-quantized weight with learnable probabilities over codewords, optimize with a representation-aware objective, and then collapse to discrete codes. We add a bit-sparsity regularizer at the bitplane level guided by per-layer Fisher/Hessian scores to adaptively prune uninformative bits, yielding mixed 1–2-bit precision per head/channel while avoiding STE bias. To stabilize large-scale training, we quantize gradients with low-variance block-orthogonal schemes and schedule pruning by matching per-layer curvature budgets. This unifies representation-aware tuning with probabilistic discrete weights and bit-sparse mixed precision, targeting the most informative subspaces to reach sub-2-bit average precision with minimal loss.

result.text: We propose an open-vocabulary multi-modal multi-label emotion recognizer that learns a language-guided prototypical hypergraph over labels and modalities, enabling zero-shot addition of new emotions. Concretely, we seed label prototypes from textual definitions/examples and jointly refine them with an EM-style ProtoNCE objective that assigns CARAT/TAILOR-style per-modality, per-label features to prototypes, while a heterogeneous hierarchical message-passing layer propagates evidence across label–modality hyperedges to capture co-occurrence and dependencies. A latent emotion memory acts as a prior over prototype mixtures to calibrate rare or partial sequences, and all modality encoders are aligned to a shared language space (as in Emotion-LLaMA) to support zero-shot transfer and natural-language explanations. We hypothesize this design improves low-resource and out-of-vocabulary emotion recognition and yields interpretable prototype-based rationales.

result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of applying diffusion probabilistic generative models to data represented as continuous functions (fields) over arbitrary metric spaces, where prior diffusion approaches require bespoke denoising networks or latent-vector representations tied to Euclidean grids. The key insight is to extend the diffusion formulation to operate directly on field parameterizations, enabling a unified end-to-end learning framework that models distributions over functions without collapsing fields into latent codes or depending on grid-based architectures. The proposed method, Diffusion Probabilistic Fields (DPF), explicitly defines forward and reverse diffusion processes in the space of fields and trains a single denoising network to predict and refine noisy field samples, allowing the same model to handle diverse modalities such as 2D images, 3D geometry, and fields on non-Euclidean metric spaces. Empirically, DPF demonstrates that a shared denoiser can successfully model these varied field distributions, removing the need for domain-specific network designs.

result.text: The paper studies the vulnerability of counterfactual explanations—used to give recourse to individuals affected by algorithmic decisions—by showing they can be manipulated via small perturbations, so ostensibly similar inputs yield drastically different recommended changes. The key insight is that lack of robustness in counterfactuals enables an attacker or model designer to create classifiers that appear fair under standard audits yet, under slight perturbations, produce much lower-cost recourse for targeted subgroups. Methodologically, the authors formalize a vulnerability framework, introduce an objective to train models that exploit this instability to reduce recourse cost for chosen groups, and empirically demonstrate on loan and violent-crime prediction datasets that certain subgroups can receive up to 20× lower-cost recourse under perturbation. These findings highlight a new failure mode for counterfactual explanations and motivate research into robust, manipulation-resistant recourse methods.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of noisy pseudo-labels in source-free domain adaptation (SFDA), where models must adapt to an unlabeled target domain without access to source data and suffer from label noise due to domain shift. Its key insight is that the label-noise distribution in SFDA is fundamentally different from conventional learning-with-noisy-labels (LLN) assumptions—making many LLN fixes ineffective—yet the early-time training phenomenon (ETP), where models first fit clean patterns before memorizing noise, still holds in SFDA. The key insight is that enforcing maximal sparsity in task-specific base predictors induces a modular allocation of latent features to tasks, which under mild conditions makes the underlying factors (a disentangled representation) identifiable and yields better generalization because each task uses only a small, relevant subset of features. To capitalize on this, the authors prove an identifiability theorem connecting sparsity and disentanglement, formulate a practical bi-level optimization that promotes sparse base predictors to learn disentangled latents, and develop a meta-learning variant using group Lasso multiclass SVMs with a tractable dual to achieve competitive few-shot performance while ensuring each task activates only a fraction of the learned representation.

result.text: The paper tackles efficient and accurate video object segmentation by improving how space-time correspondences use past frames as memory without re-encoding per-object mask features. The key insight is that inner-product affinities cause a small fixed subset of memory nodes to dominate aggregation votes, wasting memory coverage, so using negative squared Euclidean distance yields more diversified voting where every memory node can contribute. The method infers each query-frame node by associatively aggregating features from past frames using correspondence networks built on these improved affinities, which boosts memory efficiency and robustness. This simple change yields state-of-the-art results on DAVIS and YouTubeVOS while running at over 20 FPS for multiple objects.

result.text: The paper addresses how to build flow-based generative models that can handle discrete data and jointly model discrete and continuous modalities, with an application to protein sequence–structure co-design. The key insight is that the continuous-space notion of flow matching can be translated to discrete state-spaces by framing flows as Continuous Time Markov Chains (CTMCs), which yields a principled discrete analogue that subsumes discrete diffusion as a special case and improves over prior diffusion-only approaches. The method, called Discrete Flow Models (DFMs), derives training objectives and sampling procedures from CTMC flow matching to construct multimodal flows that couple discrete and continuous variables, and the authors demonstrate this framework by training a single model that jointly generates protein backbones (continuous) and amino-acid sequences (discrete), achieving state-of-the-art co-design performance while permitting flexible marginal generation of sequence or structure.

The paper addresses the underutilization of unchosen experts in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, noting that simply activating more experts can degrade output and that different routing strategies produce substantially different, non-synergistic outputs. The key insight is that unchosen experts still contain useful signals and that contrasting outputs from different activation strengths can surface better next-token probabilities without changing model weights. The authors propose Self-Contrast Mixture-of-Experts (SCMoE), a training-free, inference-time method that computes next-token probabilities by contrasting outputs produced under strong versus weak expert activation of the same MoE model, incurring minimal extra latency. Experiments on multiple benchmarks (GSM8K, StrategyQA, MBPP, HumanEval) show consistent reasoning improvements for Mixtral 8x7B—e.g., GSM8K accuracy rising from 61.79 to 66.94—and further gains when combined with self-consistency.

result.text: The paper addresses how to design a general, powerful, and scalable graph Transformer that overcomes the limited expressivity and quadratic cost of prior GTs and works across small and very large graphs. args.text: We propose a dual-equivariant Hamiltonian predictor that is simultaneously SE(3)-equivariant in real space and unitary-covariant to atomic-orbital (AO) basis rotations, addressing the brittleness of current models to basis changes. The model treats per-atom AO subspaces as (l,m)-irrep blocks endowed with U(n_l) gauge symmetry, uses equivariant local frames to tie geometry to Wigner-D actions, and performs message passing on gauge-invariant contractions while emitting gauge-covariant AO-block tensors. Angular couplings are computed via Gaunt-FFT tensor products within lightweight EGNN-style updates to avoid tensor blowup, and training enforces multi-basis consistency alongside Hermiticity and generalized-eigenproblem constraints with the overlap matrix S. This yields fast, physically consistent prediction of H/S matrices with strong cross-basis transfer and improved wavefunction initialization compared to prior SE(3)-only Hamiltonian networks.

result.text: I propose Input Sharpness-Aware Fast Adversarial Training (iSAFAT): augment single-step adversarial training with a lightweight penalty that explicitly reduces input-space sharpness within the adversarial ball. Concretely, estimate a surrogate of the dominant eigenvalue of the input Hessian by generating two FGSM-like perturbations in approximately orthogonal directions and measuring a small-radius perturbed-loss gap, then penalize this gap while aligning input gradients across these perturbations to regularize curvature without leaving the single-step regime. By directly targeting the high curvature that grows with adversarial budgets, iSAFAT mitigates the decision-boundary distortion implicated in catastrophic overfitting and stabilizes training at large epsilons. This is complementary to strong-noise FGSM variants, offering a principled curvature control mechanism at similar cost.

args.text: Communication-aware MoE scaling with overlap–granularity control: We augment granularity-based MoE scaling laws with explicit system terms for expert-parallel all-to-all communication and a measured overlap factor that quantifies how much of communication can be hidden behind computation. The model yields piecewise power-law regimes and predicts the compute- and bandwidth-optimal tuple (experts, expert width, top-k) under fixed accelerator FLOPs and interconnect budgets, with phase breaks when router load saturates or overlap regime changes. We operationalize it with a closed-loop tuner that, during training and serving, adjusts granularity and routing entropy to target a desired tokens-per-expert and overlap, and switches routing to expert-choice when predicted to improve balance/overlap. This unifies algorithmic and systems knobs into a single scaling law, improving extrapolation versus compute-only laws and enabling dynamic schedules that keep MoE models on the Pareto frontier across pretraining and heterogeneous deployments.

result.text: The paper addresses efficient long-video understanding with vision-language LLMs by tackling the computational bottleneck from vast numbers of video tokens. Its key insight is to encode videos streamingly into a small set of propagated, question-relevant memories rather than repeatedly processing all frames, preserving temporal context without excessive token cost. Methodologically, VideoStreaming segments videos into clips and uses Memory-Propagated Streaming Encoding to merge each clip with a distilled historical memory, then applies Adaptive Memory Selection to pick a constant number of question-related memories to feed the LLM for reasoning. This disentangled extraction-and-reasoning design reduces redundancy, enables precise temporal question answering, and yields improved accuracy and efficiency on long-video benchmarks.

args.text: Multi-View, Checkpoint-Ensembled Unlearnable Examples (MCE-UE) target both supervised and contrastive pretraining by optimizing a single release-time perturbation under an expectation over strong SSL augmentations and an ensemble of training checkpoints. Instead of only enforcing class separability or misclassification, we directly shape the InfoNCE/supervised objectives so that two views of the same image are repelled while each is attracted toward dynamically harvested hard negatives across checkpoints, amplifying pairwise disruption. We parameterize perturbations in a crop-stable, low-frequency local Fourier basis and penalize concentration in any single global direction, mitigating simple linear recovery like orthogonal projection. This yields unlearnable effects that transfer across training recipes and architectures, and we hypothesize improved robustness to momentum encoders by forcing persistent view-inconsistency.

result.text: The paper tackles improving GAN performance by refining consistency regularization on the discriminator, addressing the problem that naive consistency constraints can introduce visual artifacts and suboptimal synthesis quality. The key insight is that careful design of the consistency loss—avoiding alignment of augmented and unaugmented discriminator outputs in ways that force the generator to produce artifacts, and modifying how augmentations, perturbation magnitudes, and loss targets are applied—yields better training signals without degrading sample fidelity. Methodologically, the authors identify failure modes of prior consistency schemes, introduce fixes and several practical modifications (including adjusted augmentation strategies, targeted consistency targets, and regularization schedules), and validate these changes across architectures and datasets to achieve state-of-the-art FID improvements on CIFAR-10, CelebA, and ImageNet-2012.

result.text: The paper addresses inverse problems for partial differential equations that are naturally posed as mappings from operators (e.g., coefficient or boundary-condition maps) to solution functions, a setting that standard operator-learning frameworks—which map functions to functions—do not directly handle. The key insight is that by composing operator- and function-level neural architectures one can learn inverse operators directly: specifically, combining DeepONet’s branch/trunk structure for learning operator-to-function mappings with Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) components captures both local and global structure needed for stable inverse recovery. The proposed Neural Inverse Operator (NIO) architecture composes DeepONet and FNO modules in a mathematically motivated way to approximate operator→function maps, and is trained end-to-end on paired operator-function data; experiments show NIOs outperform baselines in accuracy and robustness while being orders of magnitude faster than traditional direct or PDE-constrained optimization methods.

result.text: We propose a Joint Transfer–Consistency Subspace (JTCS) detector that explicitly assumes backdoor triggers induce a shared low-dimensional activation subspace that is both highly transferable across source classes yet inconsistent under input augmentations. Concretely, we reverse-engineer a small set of candidate patterns per putative target on unlabeled inputs, then (i) quantify expected transferability across sources to that target and (ii) extract penultimate-layer subspaces spanned by triggered activations across augmented views; we score models by the affinity of these subspaces versus the augmentation-consistency gap between triggered and clean features. Attacked models exhibit a compact, high-affinity “trigger subspace” with strong ET but markedly lower feature-consistency than clean data, yielding a domain-agnostic statistic that works in two-class and multi-attack settings and remains effective against input-aware triggers whose visuals vary but converge in representation. This design sidesteps general impossibility by making its assumption explicit and testable (low-rank backdoor subspace), integrating transferability and transformation-consistency into one post-training, data-light procedure.

args.text: We propose Mixture-of-Equivariant Neural Processes (MEqNPs) that combine mixture-of-experts with steerable and convolutional NP architectures, allowing each expert to learn a different degree and type of symmetry (e.g., translation, rotation) via layer-wise partial equivariance. A permutation-invariant gating network maps the context set to mixture weights over experts and their symmetry parameters, preserving exchangeability while routing tasks or spatial regions to experts whose inductive biases match local symmetries. We encourage diverse symmetry profiles with regularizers over subgroup coefficients and add light mutual distillation across experts to share useful features without collapsing specialization, training end-to-end using the ConvNP maximum-likelihood or standard NP ELBO objectives. This design targets stochastic fields with spatially varying or task-dependent symmetries (e.g., weather, remote sensing, medical imaging), yielding coherent, calibrated predictions with improved data efficiency and robustness to symmetry mis-specification.

I propose I-P MCTS for continuous actions: each node maintains a lightweight local action policy and alternates two operators—(i) an exact entropy/KL-regularized improvement step over the continuous action space that maximizes the node’s backup objective, and (ii) a projection step that selects a small, diverse action set for progressive widening via determinantal coresets or an expected-improvement acquisition using ensemble uncertainty. This replaces heuristic PUCT with the exact optimizer, exploits local smoothness via gradient refinement of candidate actions, and scales by sampling only a few actions per node. Compared to VOOT/BOMCP, the novelty is treating action-set growth as a principled projection coupled to an exact improvement operator, unifying optimization-based MCTS with progressive widening. We amortize local policies across similar states to warm-start the improvement step and hypothesize tighter regret bounds under mild smoothness and diversity conditions.

result.text: The paper addresses the problem of making variance-reduced policy gradient (PG) methods both theoretically sound and sample-efficient without relying on an uncheckable per-iteration importance-weight assumption that prior work requires. The key insight is that a simple gradient truncation mechanism can control the instability caused by importance weights and enable variance reduction while preserving convergence guarantees, and that under policy overparameterization the problem exhibits a hidden convexity that yields faster global convergence. Building on these ideas the authors propose TSIVR-PG (Truncated Stochastic Incremental Variance-Reduced Policy Gradient), which applies truncated gradient updates within a stochastic incremental variance-reduction framework to optimize cumulative rewards or general utilities over long-term visitation distributions; they prove TSIVR-PG attains an Õ(ε⁻³) sample complexity to reach an ε-stationary policy and, under overparameterization, a global Õ(ε⁻²) sample complexity to reach an ε-optimal policy.

result.text: We propose Counterfactual Repair for Multimodal Consistency (CRMC), which detects fake news by estimating the minimal set of semantically controlled edits across text, image, and comments required to make them mutually consistent, using the resulting repair cost as a calibrated deception score. A library of atomic, modality-specific edits (e.g., entity swaps in text, localized object/attribute diffusion edits in images, and stance rewrites in comments) with learned costs is paired with a cross-modal entailment/consistency scorer to guide a planner that searches for the lowest-cost repair. We bootstrap the planner and cost model with synthetic counterfactuals derived from real samples and weak neuro-symbolic pattern supervision (manipulation, cross-modal inconsistency, repurposing), followed by adversarial self-play to generate increasingly hard inconsistencies. This yields explicit, pattern-level edit traces as explanations while better capturing cross-modal inconsistencies and comment coherence than prior multimodal detectors.

result.text: The paper addresses learning causal structure when data come from multiple domains and may include latent confounders, unifying observational and interventional datasets that vary across environments. The key insight is that multi-domain observational data can be viewed as interventional data with unknown targets in a single domain, and that causal invariances expressible via do-calculus yield an S-Markov property linking interventional distributions across domains to graphical criteria on a selection diagram. Building on this, the authors propose S-FCI, a constraint-based causal discovery algorithm that uses the S-Markov constraints to infer causal relations from combined observational and interventional multi-domain data, and they prove S-FCI is sound and generalizes existing constraint-based methods.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of unreliable and untraceable outputs in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models (RALMs), where irrelevant retrieved documents and missing citations can harm answer quality and trustworthiness. Its key insight is that the language model’s own step-by-step reasoning trajectories can be used to both filter retrieved evidence for relevance and to produce verifiable citations, improving reliability and traceability. The proposed self-reasoning framework generates reasoning trajectories via a relevance-aware process to select candidate documents, an evidence-aware selective process to choose supporting passages, and a trajectory analysis process to synthesize answers and citations; this pipeline was evaluated on four public datasets and outperformed prior methods, reaching GPT-4–comparable performance with only 2,000 training samples.

args.text: We propose a shot-aware hierarchical video-to-music system that first plans a long-horizon symbolic score aligned to video—tempo/beat curve, section boundaries, chord/mode trajectory, and motif tokens—then renders audio with a fast rectified-flow spectrogram generator. The planner uses LORIS-like context encoders over minutes of visual rhythm and events, but predicts discrete score tokens with a DanceFormer-inspired beat-first decomposition; the actor conditions on both the plan and CAVP-style visual embeddings, and supports optional text/style prompts via a CoDi-like composable interface. During sampling, we apply lightweight joint discriminator guidance to correct cross-modal misalignment and tighten audiovisual synchronization, yielding high fidelity without training a full multimodal model end-to-end. Trained on in-the-wild video–music pairs with weak labels for harmony/structure, this architecture targets stronger long-term rhythmic alignment and thematic consistency than prior V2A/V2M systems.

result.text: We propose LAMP: a layout-to-action multimodal program inducer that, given a UI/web screenshot and a natural-language instruction, jointly predicts HTML/CSS code and an executable interaction program whose actions (e.g., click, type, scroll) are grounded to the predicted DOM via selectors, enabling end-to-end automation and accessibility. LAMP builds on screenshot-to-HTML pretraining and instruction-tuned web-to-code for faithful code synthesis, augments with an instruction-aware visual querying module and a focus-conditioned pathway to localize task-relevant regions, and trains with render-and-compare consistency plus script-execution feedback. Structurally, it first predicts a coarse region-level layout skeleton before completing HTML-like DSL code, then compiles action primitives against the induced DOM. We hypothesize this yields stronger generalization and robustness on multi-step UI tasks than vision-only or code-only baselines.

args.text: Physio-ROI Diff-ODE is a disease-conditioned multi-lead ECG generator that couples a latent neural ODE of vectorcardiogram dynamics with a differentiable lead-field projection and a region-disentangled diffusion refiner focused on P/QRS/T segments. Temporal disease conditioning is injected via localized control signals and trained with a multi-lead view discriminator, while a cross-lead masked reconstruction auxiliary task enforces spatio-temporal coherence. A simulator-in-the-loop regularizer aligns the learned ODE with physiologic priors and exposes controllable parameterized sampling for counterfactual edits. The hybrid model targets high-fidelity, label-preserving augmentation and improved generalization across lead subsets compared to pure GAN or diffusion baselines.

result.text: The paper addresses the overlooked availability threat in autonomous driving camera perception—specifically attacks that increase perception latency to create dangerous system-level effects—rather than merely causing misclassification. The key insight is that by crafting adversarial inputs optimized not just for incorrect outputs but for increasing execution time across the entire camera-based perception pipeline, an attacker can amplify downstream safety failures (e.g., crashes) far beyond prior object-detection–focused latency attacks. The authors propose SlowTrack, a two-stage attack framework with three novel loss functions that jointly target perception runtime and imperceptibility, and they evaluate it across four popular perception pipelines as well as on the Baidu Apollo stack and LGSVL simulator. Results show SlowTrack substantially increases perception latency and system-level harm—raising crash rates to about 95% on average—while maintaining comparable visual stealth to existing attacks.

We formalize sequential design with performativity as an MDP whose transition dynamics encode endogenous distribution shifts induced by deployments, and target equilibria by augmenting the reward with stability/consistency terms. args.text: Granularity-annealed MoE: an online coarsening schedule that adaptively merges small experts into larger ones during training to remain on the compute-optimal scaling frontier. The method is unsupervised and model-agnostic: it uses only a single pretrained language model without any fine-tuning or architecture changes, generates or identifies semantically related candidate outputs for a prompt, and computes entropy over their aggregated probabilities to produce a calibrated uncertainty score; experiments and ablations show this score predicts QA accuracy better than standard baselines.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of performing inverse graphics and extracting interpretable 3D structure from monocular images without requiring multi-view datasets, by bridging image GANs and differentiable rendering. args.text: UniSelect is a task- and query-conditioned submodular frame subset learner that unifies sparse video perception across classification, captioning, QA, and summarization under a fixed compute budget. It learns per-frame informativeness and pairwise diversity in a shared multimodal transformer conditioned on text queries, distills from full-context teachers, and leverages large-scale implicit importance signals and dense differential captions for supervision, while a hierarchical selector enforces temporal coherence via multi-resolution constraints. At test time, UniSelect supports any-subset refinement: it actively acquires additional frames where uncertainty remains and can impute skipped context with a lightweight temporal prior, yielding consistent accuracy gains with 5–10× fewer processed frames. This builds on joint frame selection, RL-based selective watching, language-guided saliency, robust highlight labels, dense differential captioning, and temporally aware semi-supervision.

Patch-Cage NeRF augments cage-based deformation of radiance fields with a learned local prior to better preserve thin structures and realistic material responses. We represent geometry with a neural SDF and compose the cage mapping with a residual deformation field predicted by a set of 3D surface-anchored latent kernels that are retrieved and blended from a learned multi-scale patch dictionary. A transformer attends from handle/cage motions and local SDF features to place and blend these kernels, trained end-to-end with multiview photometric loss plus ARAP/curvature regularization on SDF level sets and optional supervision from deforming-shape datasets. This yields category-agnostic, controllable edits that maintain high-frequency detail and improve deformation transfer across novel objects.

result.text: The paper studies how semantic attention mechanisms can emerge in dot-product self-attention by theoretically analyzing a solvable non-linear attention model with tied low-rank query and key matrices; it addresses why and when training produces positional vs. semantic attention. The key insight is that, in a high-dimensional, large-sample asymptotic regime, the nonconvex empirical loss has a globally optimal solution that is provably either positional (tokens attend by position) or semantic (tokens attend by meaning), and increasing sample complexity induces a sharp phase transition from positional to semantic solutions. args.text: We propose CoreConCut: a core-contraction–guided cut-selection policy for core-guided pseudo-Boolean MaxSAT that learns to pick and order PB cuts to maximally shrink the current multiset of unsatisfiable cores. The key signal is a core-contraction reward defined as the predicted reduction in a weighted minimum hitting set objective over recent cores; we train a hierarchical policy (first predict how many cuts, then select an ordered subset) to imitate a lookahead expert that evaluates true contraction via short rollouts. The policy featurizes core structure (literal/relaxation-variable frequencies and co-occurrence motifs) and candidate cuts, and is integrated into the PB bound-refinement loop to alternate contraction- and bound-oriented phases for faster convergence. For the gray-zone, we run a brief probing phase that applies temporary masks and uses an upper-confidence-bound policy to estimate each channel’s marginal loss impact, prioritizing probes for channels whose feature maps are redundant with others to resolve ambiguity. This uncertainty-aware deferral reduces mistaken removals among near-tied candidates and explicitly breaks redundancy, yielding more reliable structured pruning without heavy hyperparameter search.

args.text: We propose amortized latent gradient-flow refinement for pretrained generators: learn a small neural flow T that maps base latents to refined latents in one forward pass, trained to mimic the endpoint of discriminator-driven gradient dynamics defined by the combined prior-plus-discriminator energy. Concretely, we distill short stochastic refinement rollouts (e.g., latent Langevin or DGflow-style trajectories) into T via path-matching and distributional losses under the target energy, while adding Jacobian/Lipschitz regularization to preserve support and ensure stable, contraction-like updates. At inference, composing T with the frozen generator yields the quality gains of iterative discriminator-guided refinement at near feedforward speed, and T can be updated online as the critic/energy evolves. This bridges energy reweighting and latent MCMC with an amortized, deployment-friendly module that accelerates post-hoc sample improvement without retraining the generator.

result.text: The paper addresses the challenge of realistically swapping objects in videos when those objects are being manipulated by hands, a scenario where existing diffusion-based video editors struggle because they do not model changes in hand-object interaction (HOI) caused by differences in object shape or function. The key insight is that realistic object swaps require HOI awareness and temporally consistent motion propagation: a model must both adapt the hand grasp and interaction patterns to the new object in a reference frame and then coherently extend that edited state through the video. HOI-Swap implements this in two stages—first training a diffusion model self-supervised to perform single-frame object swaps with learned HOI adjustments, and then propagating the edit across the sequence by warping the stage-I edited frame according to sampled motion points and conditioning a video-generation diffusion model on this warped sequence to achieve controllable motion alignment—resulting in more realistic, temporally consistent edits than prior methods.

result.text: This paper tackles off-policy evaluation (OPE) for partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with unobserved confounders, where the evaluation policy acts on observables but the behavior policy depends on latent states—an area where prior work either ignores confounding or assumes tabular structure. The key insight is that one can identify the target policy’s value via bridge functions that relate the unobserved-state-dependent quantities to the observable-data distribution, enabling valid OPE despite latent confounding. The authors propose a minimax learning framework to estimate these bridge functions under general function approximation, and derive three practical estimators—value-function-based, marginalized importance-sampling, and doubly robust—built from the learned bridges. They also provide detailed nonasymptotic and asymptotic analyses showing the estimators’ theoretical properties, making the approach applicable to continuous or large observation/state spaces.

args.text: I propose Fractional Positive-Negative Momentum (FPNM), an optimizer that restores the beneficial heavy-tailed, anisotropic stochastic gradient noise suppressed by adaptive methods while retaining their speed. FPNM maintains paired positive/negative momentum buffers but replaces exponential averaging with a power-law (fractional) memory kernel, calibrated per layer via an online tail-index estimator, so that the buffer-difference emulates alpha-stable noise with a target heaviness that encourages fast saddle escape and flat-minima selection. The scheme plugs into SGD or Adam by swapping their EMA momentum with a multi-timescale fractional EMA and lightly clipping only extreme buffer differences for stability, yielding a discrete dynamics that approximates a Lévy-driven SDE whose stationary behavior aligns with Gibbs under heavy-tailed perturbations. We hypothesize this preserves Adam-like optimization speed while recovering SGD-like generalization, especially in regimes with small batches or sharp basins.

result.text: The paper addresses how to enable large language models (LLMs) to perform reasoning over graph-structured data by encoding graphs as text, identifying why naive conversions fail and which design choices matter. Its key insight is that LLM performance depends critically not just on the downstream task but on the specific textual encoding of the graph and on intrinsic graph structural properties, so that different encoders suit different tasks and graph types. Methodologically, the authors systematically evaluate a palette of graph-to-text encoders across diverse graph reasoning tasks and graph structures, analyze interactions between encoder, task, and graph topology, and demonstrate that choosing appropriate encodings can substantially improve LLM accuracy (by 4.8%–61.8%) on graph reasoning benchmarks.

args.text: We propose Algebraic-Diffusion IP-IRM, which augments iterative partition-based invariance with unsupervised discovery of continuous symmetries. We learn a small set of Lie-algebra generators in feature space from local view pairs, build a diffusion operator to estimate invariant subspaces and orbits, and alternate between (i) partitioning by orbit components to enforce subset-invariance and (ii) sparsifying cross-subspace interactions while applying a factorized-support regularizer to decouple correlated factors. This yields modular, approximately group-equivariant latents without prespecified groups, and ties downstream predictors to sparse subsets of generators/subspaces to enhance identifiability and OOD transfer. We hypothesize that the learned generators converge to true data symmetries when present and to approximate stabilizers otherwise, improving disentanglement and transfer on correlated-factor benchmarks while enabling plug-and-play equivariant layers.

args.text: We propose a protein-conditioned RNA co-design model that uses a discrete–continuous CTMC flow to jointly generate RNA sequence, base-pairing matrices (including pseudoknots), and 3D coordinates as an ensemble conditioned on the protein interface. The model integrates an inverse-folding–guided flow with a frozen RosettaFold2NA complex predictor for score-distillation-style guidance to enforce structural fidelity without expensive co-training, while embedding differentiable projection layers to enforce RNA secondary-structure constraints during the flow. The discrete jump process employs biologically informed nucleotide replacement kernels that respect base-pair compatibility during noising to improve sampling efficiency, and training uses flow matching to target ensemble distributions rather than single structures. This unifies inverse folding + flow matching with CTMC flows over mixed discrete/continuous variables and learned constraint enforcement, enabling faster, higher-fidelity protein-conditioned RNA design.

We propose Uncertainty- and TD-error-aware Expert-Choice MoE for value-based RL: a soft MoE value network whose routing uses a combination of epistemic uncertainty (via bootstrapped Q-head variance) and per-sample TD-error to assign states to specialized experts, with expert-choice routing to ensure balanced utilization and allow variable expert counts per token. To reduce destructive interference as targets drift, each expert’s features are regularized toward their initialization (InFeR) while expert outputs are encouraged to be mutually orthogonal, promoting a compact, diverse shared subspace that can scale stably. Compared to standard soft top-k routing, this design should yield better scaling curves by focusing capacity on uncertain or high-error regions, improving data efficiency and stability in both online Atari/DMControl and offline D4RL. Ablations would isolate the benefits of uncertainty-aware gating, expert-choice load balancing, and orthogonality/initialization regularizers.

args.text: We propose TC-Conformal: a history-aware, logic-augmented conformal forecasting framework for temporal knowledge graphs that produces calibrated tail sets and time-interval predictions. A contrastive detector first estimates whether a query is history-driven, then routes scoring to (i) a time-aware copy/generation expert fused with temporal logical rule reasoning for repetitive patterns and interval prediction, or (ii) a parametric temporal embedding expert for novel, non-recurrent cases. To deliver reliable coverage under graph-temporal dependence and drift, we perform split conformal calibration with relation- and recency-weighted nonconformity scores computed over temporally local neighborhoods, extending weighted conformal prediction on graphs. The result is guaranteed-coverage predictions with interpretable rule justifications, tighter sets for novelty-driven queries, and higher accuracy on history-driven cases.

The authors create QH9, a large dataset of precise Hamiltonian matrices for 130,831 QM9-derived geometries and nearly 1k–3k molecular dynamics trajectories, and design benchmark tasks plus baseline ML models to demonstrate predictive capacity; they release the dataset and code as an open benchmark to spur further method development.

args.text: We propose Movement-Aware Layer-Adaptive Hardware-Constrained Pruning (MALAH), a fine-tuning-time pruning method that meets device latency/memory budgets while preserving accuracy. MALAH forms a per-weight importance score by blending L2-distortion-aware magnitude rescaling with a movement signal accumulated during fine-tuning, then aggregates these scores to channel/group units and enforces hardware-friendly structure via lightweight re-grouping. At regular intervals, it solves a latency-LUT–guided knapsack to prune or restore groups to the target budget, with a feedback mechanism that can unprune groups whose movement indicates rising importance. This joint signal and structure approach aims to outperform purely magnitude-, movement-, or latency-driven baselines under strict budget constraints across vision and language models.

We propose iEF-NG-AL, a curvature-aware active learning method that scores candidates by their predicted reduction in validation loss after a one-step natural-gradient update, using the improved empirical Fisher (iEF) as a scalable preconditioner. This unifies GLISTER’s validation-loss lookahead with BAIT’s Fisher-informed selection, and scales to massive batches by first ranking via uncertainty/influence and then selecting a diverse subset under the natural-gradient metric using a fast diversification strategy. A streaming variant maintains iEF statistics over a sliding window and queries on-the-fly with the same NG-diversity objective, enabling budget-controlled decisions without hand-tuning. We hypothesize this yields better label-efficiency and stability than EF-based or purely heuristic AL, especially under distribution shift and large-batch regimes.

We propose Fractional-Dilation Convolution (FracDilConv), a continuous, differentiable generalization of dilated convolution that parameterizes receptive-field expansion via learnable orders of the fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) and chirp-like spectral envelopes. Unlike fixed or discretely learned tap spacings, FracDilConv morphs the effective sampling lattice by modulating FRFT order per layer/channel while controlling frequency content for stable gradients, combining the expressive tap-placement flexibility of DCLS with the bandwidth-aware kernel parameterization of FlexConv. Implemented with FlashFFTConv-style fused block-matmul FFT/FRFT kernels, FracDilConv yields fast training/inference and serves as a drop-in replacement for conv/DC layers. FracDilConv also turns dilation/kernel-size choices into a low-dimensional continuous manifold, enabling faster, smoother architecture search (e.g., replacing discrete op choices in DASH) and promising better multi-scale modeling in vision and operator-learning tasks.

result.text: EdgeDecentGS: a fully decentralized, fault-tolerant training framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting on heterogeneous, intermittently connected devices. It adopts DOGS-style spatial decomposition but replaces the master-driven ADMM with boundary-only consensus performed via scheduled one-peer exponential graphs and Moshpit-style averaging, enabling near-exact model alignment without a reliable high-speed fabric. Communication is further reduced by Grendel’s sparsity—nodes gossip only Gaussians whose screen-space footprints intersect neighbors’ pixel shards—and by LEAD-style compressed exchanges with error-corrected tracking, stabilizing optimization under heavy quantization. This yields city-scale 3DGS that scales beyond single clusters, preserving quality while improving wall-clock convergence under churn and load imbalance.

result.text: The paper tackles the problem of representation gap in knowledge distillation, where student models produce noisier features than teachers, harming transfer of knowledge across tasks and architectures. The key insight is that many complex KD strategies essentially aim to discard noise and retain valuable feature information, so explicitly denoising student features before matching them to teacher features should improve distillation. The authors propose DiffKD, which trains a diffusion model on teacher features to denoise student features and then distills between the refined student features and teacher features; to make this practical they use a lightweight diffusion design with a linear autoencoder and an adaptive noise-matching module to align student noise levels with the diffusion process. Extensive experiments across classification, detection, and segmentation show DiffKD consistently improves performance and yields state-of-the-art results.
